analysis:
The two supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1574-2125), which hold historical release notes only. The patch excerpt shows documentation-only changes at the top of the file: a new v0.10.8 candidate section (head lines 11-333) replaces the v0.10.7 heading. No code, configuration, or mode changes were supplied. I found no security regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption in the visible text.

The base text describes earlier behavior that touches the retained threat T-041 (SSD prefix cache), A-008 and TB-002 (heartbeat detail fields, coordinator wire). Examples are balanced checkpoint quantization, a deeper write queue (six jobs under the existing byte caps), a cache-key replacement after Secure Enclave key repair, and a cache-status `detail` field that exposes only coarse causes such as `key_unavailable`. Those entries describe past releases and were not modified by this PR. They are not new claims in this change.

The changelog also records `logprobs` and log lines that avoid request text, which is consistent with the data-exposure assumptions. I cannot check these claims against source.

The head-side v0.10.8 text is mostly outside the supplied units; only the patch excerpt's start (the pair-update and rollout notes) was visible and it was truncated. Cluster pairing, auto-update and coordinator approval-cap behavior (a pair on 0.10.6 stopping service once 0.10.8 registers) therefore remain unexamined. Whether the 0.10.8 source changes weaken any retained threat (T-043 watchdog/rollback, T-041 cache) cannot be determined from this batch. A later pass should review the actual code changes behind the changelog, in particular the update, pairing and cache logic, rather than treat this documentation review as clearing them.
